title: He led over 2,000 miners and laborers across a border - and got arrested for it. Twice.

sources.text: South African History Online - Mohandas K. Gandhi arrested as he leads march of Indian miners
Byju's - This Day in History, November 6

caption:
He led over 2,000 miners and laborers across a border - and got arrested for it. Twice.

The non-violent march protested a discriminatory £3 tax on former indentured Indians and a law invalidating Hindu and Muslim marriages. Gandhi was arrested that day, released on bail, rejoined the march and was arrested again.

It was one of the defining early demonstrations of organized, non-violent mass resistance - a method Gandhi would later bring home to India's own independence movement.

The Volksrust march is a reminder that India's influence on global movements for justice predates its own independence by decades.
